evidence.note: Ran a deliberately tiny smoke test (ITERS=2, LAYERS=2, DIM=128) to cheaply validate the full pipeline/checkpoint path before spending on real training — reserving cheap compute for validation.
Tested 17- vs 18-layer checkpoint sizes and chose the largest model (31MB) that fits the 32MB cap, sizing the main run's capacity to the constraint before committing.
Committed main budget to a 10k-iter run, tracking val_bpb against an estimated target loss (~2.63) at each validation — a right-sized main run monitored toward the goal.
After the main run barely passed (0.9829), added a targeted low-LR continuation-tuning phase to build margin (down to 0.9775), adjusting allocation reactively as results arrived.
Reserved a final verification pass (size, forward/loss contract, loaded-checkpoint bpb) before submitting rather than over-spending on more training.

reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated budget across phases — cheap end-to-end smoke validation, a main run sized to the byte cap, and a targeted continuation-tuning phase — and adjusted allocation as results came in (adding continuation for margin after a razor-thin pass), matching anchor 8. It stops short of 10 because it never ran small probes to estimate the steps/capacity needed to cross the threshold: the 10k-iteration length was chosen without a scaling probe and capacity was simply maxed to the size cap, so the main-run sizing rested on constraint-fitting rather than probe-derived evidence.
